title: SDK integration walkthrough - Meridian Retail
topics: Auth and env vars (API key vs SSO)
Console walkthrough: API keys, projects, routes
summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Meridian Retail through Python and TypeScript SDK quickstarts, auth patterns (API key env var vs SSO/Service accounts), Console flows for keys/projects, and Optimize recommendations (batching, KV cache, quantization). Customer is evaluating hosted API vs dedicated for privacy/legal; security engineer asked about KMS and audit logs. Agreed to run a small pilot and share security docs and pricing.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-10-10 14:00 PT | Duration 48m | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Alex Chen (Meridian CTO), Maya Rivera (Lead Engineer), Samir Patel (Security)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for carving out time today, quick intros — I'm Jordan on the AE side, priya's our solutions engineer, we'll run through SDK quickstarts in python and typescript then flip to the console and some optimize recs.
[00:18] Alex: thanks, excited — timeline we're looking at is a 6 week pilot, want to validate latency and PII handling.
[00:26] Priya: great, we'll keep that in mind; quick note on roles — Samir if you want to flag anything security we can stop and deep dive.
[00:34] Samir: yeah please call out KMS, audit logs, retention, and SAML/SSO options.
[00:40] Priya: absolutely. Ok first, python quickstart — there's a pip package we surface (it's redwood-inference in the quickstart) so typical flow is pip install redwood-inference then set env var REDWOOD_API_KEY. In code you'd do something like: from redwood import Client; client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')) then client.generate(prompt=...) — that's the gist.
[01:05] Maya: is there a typed client for typescript or node?
[01:09] Jordan: yes we have an npm package @redwood/inference, same patterns: set process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, import RedwoodClient from '@redwood/inference', then await client.responses.create or client.chat.stream depending on streaming. The surface is intentionally similar across languages.
[01:28] Priya: demoing a quick snippet now — bear with me while I paste the quickstart. (screen share) here's python example: 1) install, 2) export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_xxx, 3) run a simple prompt. We also show a local env file example for dev.
[01:47] Alex: question — storing API keys in env is fine for dev, what do you recommend for production?
[01:53] Priya: for prod we recommend using a secrets store (KMS/Hashi Vault) and rotating keys. For Private deployments you can use customer-managed KMS or HSM; for Hosted we support envelope encryption and integration with major KMS providers.
[02:10] Samir: can you point me to where audit logs live?
[02:13] Jordan: in the console under Settings -> Audit logs, and we stream events to your SIEM via delivered webhooks or S3 exports. We'll share the SOC2 section in the security pack.
[02:24] Priya: switching to typescript quickstart — here's the minimal flow: import client, set up request, handle streaming chunks via onDelta callbacks, and handle function/tool-calling payloads. Note transcripts may say onDalta sometimes in logs (transcription error).
[02:44] Maya: for streaming responses how do we handle partial tokens and cancellations?
[02:48] Priya: the SDK exposes a stream object with cancel() and on('delta',...) events; we also have built-in retry logic and backpressure controls. For high throughput we recommend batching in the SDK layer or using our built-in batch endpoints.
[03:05] Jordan: quick console walkthrough — Projects > Routes, create an API key scoped to only the endpoints you need, set rate limits and quotas, and generate a key for the pilot. You can also pin model versions per route to lock behavior.
[03:24] Alex: model pinning — useful. Any notes on quantization or cost controls?
[03:28] Priya: yes, that's where Redwood Optimize comes in. We surface recommended quantization profiles per model, and suggested batch sizes based on your latency SLOs. For example for short customer chat messages we recommended q4_0_quantized for a good cost/latency compromise. Also enable prefix/KV cache for repeated context to cut token costs.
[03:51] Samir: prefix cache — is that stored in our VPC for Private?
[03:55] Priya: for Private yes, KV cache is customer-local. For Hosted we encrypt at rest and you can set TTLs and retention policies.
[04:04] Jordan: moving back to integration patterns — authentication options: 1) API key per service account (easiest), 2) SAML/SO S integration for console SSO and role mapping, 3) mTLS or private networking for dedicated instances.
[04:20] Maya: do you have service account tokens for CI/CD?
[04:23] Priya: yes you can create scoped service keys in the console and set an expiration or rotate them automatically.
[04:30] Alex: infra questions — if we go dedicated, is there a network egress requirement?
[04:33] Jordan: Dedicated can be deployed into your VPC with no public egress, or we can provide a private peering connection; we also have an on-prem package for air-gapped environments.
[04:45] Priya: now I'll run a small end-to-end demo: python client calling the hosted route, then show the same TypeScript call running in node. (starts demo) — note: slight lag while my workspace spins up, transcription may drop words.
[05:12] Priya: here you can see responses.stream yielding chunked deltas; when we detect function/tool calling we return structured JSON that can be passed to your backend for execution.
[05:33] Maya: for structured outputs do you recommend using function-calling or output schema enforcement?
[05:38] Priya: both — function-calling for invoking external actions, and structured output + JSON schema validation for deterministic responses. We also have response hooks in the SDK to validate shapes before committing.
[05:52] Alex: what about latency numbers — can you share ballpark for small prompts vs lengthy convo?
[05:58] Jordan: ballpark on p95 for a 128-token prompt on a hosted standard model is ~120-200ms for optimized runtimes; long context or larger models will increase that. We'll run benchs with your sample prompts.
[06:13] Samir: security checklist — do you support SSO with SCIM provisioning and role-based access?
[06:18] Jordan: yes SSO via SAML or OIDC, and SCIM provisioning for user sync; RBAC is customizable per project.
[06:26] Priya: circling back to cost controls — you can set per-route quotas and alerts in the console; Optimize also provides batching suggestions and cache TTLs. We'll upload a sample cost modeling sheet for your usage pattern.
[06:43] Maya: curious about SDK versions — what is backwards compat story?
[06:47] Priya: semver, we keep a compatibility matrix published in the docs, and the console warns on deprecated routes. For major changes we publish migration guides.
[06:57] Jordan: ok let's talk pilot scope — we propose a 2-week perf pilot using your staging data, run 3 workloads: chat assist, product search rerank (embeddings), and batch nightly summarization. We'll measure latency, cost per 1k tokens, and quality regression.
[07:17] Alex: that sounds good. What's required from our side?
[07:20] Jordan: provide sample prompt sets, small dataset for reranking, and a contact for infra to set up keys or dedicated VPC if you choose. We'll supply an onboarding runbook.
[07:29] Samir: send the security whitepaper and SOC2, ISO docs. Also need KMS integration details.
[07:34] Jordan: will do.
[07:36] Priya: quick callouts — common pitfalls we see: 1) not pinning model versions before a pilot, 2) underestimating token growth in conversational apps, 3) forgetting batching for high throughput endpoints. We add guardrails in the console to help.
[07:51] Maya: for the Node quickstart, any gotchas around TypeScript types?
[07:55] Priya: import types from @redwood/inference/types and we include example d.ts in the package. If you use bundlers, ensure streaming isn't polyfilled incorrectly.
[08:07] Jordan: end of call recap: we'll share pricing and pilot proposal, security docs, quickstart snippets, and set up a follow-up to kick off the pilot week of Oct 18.
[08:20] Alex: can we get a short checklist for infra so we can provision before the kickoff?
[08:24] Jordan: yes checklist + sample terraform snippets, we'll attach to the follow-up.
[08:30] Maya: thanks — one more question on logs, will request-level logs include user identifiers or are they pseudonymized?
[08:36] Samir: tagging on that — we need controls for PII redaction.
[08:39] Priya: logs can be configured — we can pseudonymize or strip PII at ingest for hosted; private/offline stores give you full control. We'll share config options.
[08:50] Jordan: ok wrapping up, thanks everyone. We'll send materials and action items now.
[09:00] (call ends)
